spans.text: The DGR units, of which there are various types, were attempts by Copehtor to reproduce the full might of the Sword of Damocles in case the Grand Primaries ever returned. The units are given prototype numbers beginning at 001 and going as high as 034, though most of the units no longer exist. The initial three units, DGR-001 through 003, are the most ambitious attempts, standing above giants. Units made beyond that abandoned the need to gesture toward the Sword of Damocles’ scale, though are still massive by most standards and stand on par with most giants. These frame units, colloquially called DAGGERS, are mostly built to have a framebilt pilot integrated into them to act as their operator and pilot. The first three DGR units, referred to as ProtoDGRs, were themselves sentient in the same sense as the Sword of Damocles, and could function as long as they had some connection to a qualifying operator.

Most of the DGR units were deployed into the atmosphere alongside the Sword of Damocles, and were destroyed by the same use of Lycrothemia’s Lunar Devastation that rendered the Sword itself inoperable. Most of the basic DGR units were destroyed, and the ProtoDGRs were sent crashing back down to the planet in disrepair. The final act that the Sword of Damocles took was to force their Astral Transmission Drives to activate and send them home to the Cauldron, where rebel nephilim and framebilt restored them and left them dormant. The nephilim of the Cauldron possess an activation device for each, known as their PMLs that can force them into activity to act as guardians of the territory if necessary.
DGRs do not require food, drink or air.

DGR frame units are created to combat interplanar beings and the agents of deities, so they are equipped with a technology that prevents planar displacement. This also protects (and traps) the pilots of the units, preventing teleportation of any kind in or out of a DGR unit’s internal compartments and warding against ethereal creatures moving through them. Unless the DGR unit is willing to subject itself to the effect, its pilot and occupants are immune to any effect that would move them to a different plane - this includes demiplanes, and effects that create them such as the
spell. However, effects that teleport them within the same plane can still affect them, and effects that teleport them also teleport their occupants.

Many other types of DGR frame units were created at much smaller scales, and were not made of pure thecite like those that came before (but many do have an alloy with a roughly 5% thecite purity). They were deployed alongside the Sword of Damocles and the ProtoDGRs, and were mostly blown from the sky at the same time. Unlike their larger forebears, most of them weren’t durable enough to survive Lycrothemia’s Lunar Devastation, so most of these mass-produced DGRs were destroyed. Some lucky ones were broken and scattered across Somnus Domina, where they fell to the planet like meteors and buried themselves in the earth. Unlaunched units remained in the Cauldron, but were scattered by the early nephilim to avoid their discovery, in hopes that they could be used again in the future.

These DGR units also have PML badges that could be used to pilot them, but like all DGRs were constructed to respond to the presence of an eidolos, be they in sepherite or eidolic armament form. An eidolos could temporarily reduce themselves to their sepherite to merge with such a unit, modifying its output and taking control of it. This tactic was designed to give the eidolos of the Twilight Sentinels greater mobility in the war to come, but never saw proper use. A pilot wielding an eidolic armament can command and pilot these lesser DGR units, but since they lack the will of the eidolos, the DGR unit’s own compliance is necessary to do so. Simply being around an eidolic armament is enough to return them to activity.

These smaller frame units could exhibit personalities and sapience, but for the most part remain dormant unless in the presence of a PML or eidolos. They communicate only when addressed, and for the most part only give strictly utilitarian answers. These DGRs have an innately protective nature: if they find reason to be active, they more often than not protect anything not designated as their enemies from harm. They are largely incapable of forming complex opinions, though they have strong pattern recognition capabilities.

Though DGR units fall into their listed size categories, the full height and size of them often exceeds their size category. Their existing size categories function to make them usable in a regular gaming environment and on a battle grid. Elements like DGR units, the Sword of Damocles, and other constructs made during the Age of Sunderance clash heavily with the modern culture of Somnus Domina, and certainly don’t represent the typical level of technology reached by the world at large (with the exception of the advanced level of technology available in High Wave). They are representative of the desperation and level of conflict reached during the battle against the Grand Primaries, when the Eidolons and forces of the mortal world discarded any pretense of prudence as they developed more powerful means to fight their impossible enemy. When the war ended, elements like the DGRs are one of the reasons that vaults were built and much information was kept secret: given hindsight, the Eidolons regret achieving this level of destructive potential and hope to keep it buried.
